title: The Pile: 800GB of Diverse Text
hook: Web text alone leaves gaps. The Pile stitches together 22 curated sources — academic and professional — so a language model picks up knowledge plain web crawls miss.
key_points: An 800GB English corpus built from 22 diverse, high-quality subsets.
Mixes academic and professional sources to broaden cross-domain knowledge.
GPT-2 and GPT-3 struggle on some of its domains, such as academic writing.
Models trained on it improve on both in-domain and downstream evaluations.
Built by EleutherAI and widely used to train open LLMs.
content_html: Leo Gao, Stella Biderman, Sid Black, and colleagues at EleutherAI built the Pile, an 800GB English text corpus assembled from 22 diverse, high-quality subsets drawn from academic and professional sources. The goal is to broaden a model's cross-domain knowledge beyond what plain web text provides.
extra_html:
What it is

The corpus deliberately mixes specialized domains rather than relying on generic web crawls. When the authors evaluate GPT-2 and GPT-3 on its components, the models struggle on some domains — academic writing among them — revealing gaps in what web-trained models have seen. Models trained on the Pile improve on both in-domain and downstream evaluations.

Why it matters

The Pile became a go-to corpus for training open large language models, giving the community a shared, documented dataset to work from. Its emphasis on diverse, curated sources reflects a broader lesson: what you train on shapes what a model knows, and breadth of domains is part of the recipe.

related.title: GPT-3: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
related.hook: Show the model a few examples right in the prompt and it picks up the task — no fine-tuning, no gradient updates. GPT-3 turned prompting into the new programming.

related.title: Deduplicating Training Data Makes LMs Better
related.hook: Training corpora are full of copies — one 61-word sentence shows up 60,000+ times in C4. Strip the duplicates and models memorize far less and evaluate more honestly.
